Hazardous.title: plastic Bottles
steps: Collect all used plastic bottles from home and separate them from other waste like cans, glass, or food scraps.
Rinse the bottles to remove leftover liquids or residue to prevent contamination in the recycling process.
Remove caps and labels if required by your local recycling guidelines.
Sort by type if possible (e.g., separate PET bottles from other plastics) to help recycling centers process them efficiently.
Bundle or bag the bottles in a plastic bag or cardboard box to keep them contained for easy transport.
Locate a nearby recycling center or collection point using online resources or local apps. Some grocery stores or municipal centers have dedicated bins.
Transport the prepared bottles to the recycling center following any center-specific instructions.
Hand over the bottles to the staff or place them in the designated bin for PET/plastic bottles.
Verify with staff if the bottles are accepted for recycling to ensure proper disposal.
Encourage family and neighbors to follow this process to reduce plastic waste collectively.
precautions: Do not burn plastic bottles as it releases toxic fumes.
Avoid mixing plastics with hazardous or organic waste.
Do not throw plastic bottles in regular trash if recycling options are available.
Follow the guidelines of the recycling center carefully.
Store bottles safely before drop-off to avoid leaks or contamination.

Hazardous.title: Batteries
steps: Collect all types of used batteries (AA, AAA, button cells, rechargeable, etc.) from home and keep them separate from other household waste.
Place batteries in a sealed, non-metal container (like a plastic box) to prevent short circuits. Store away from children, pets, and heat sources.

Check local guidelines: some areas require different types of batteries (alkaline, lithium, rechargeable) to be collected separately. Verify instructions from your local recycling center or municipality.
Locate a recycling center using online tools, apps, or your municipality website. Some supermarkets and electronic stores have designated battery collection bins.
Carry your stored batteries carefully to avoid damage or leaks. Keep the container upright and secure during transport.
At the recycling center, hand over the batteries to staff or place them in the designated battery recycling bin. Ensure the center accepts your battery types.
Verify acceptance if unsure and encourage friends and family to recycle batteries properly.
precautions: Never throw batteries in regular trash.
Do not burn or puncture batteries, as they can leak toxic chemicals or explode.
Keep batteries away from water or high heat.
Separate different types of batteries when required by local guidelines.
Store batteries safely before transport to avoid leaks or short circuits.

E-Waste.title: How to Properly Recycle E-Waste
steps: Do not throw electronic devices in household trash.
Collect devices like phones, chargers, computers, and old TVs separately.
Remove personal data from devices before disposal.
Take e-waste to certified recycling centers to safely recover valuable materials.
Spread awareness in your community about the importance of proper e-waste disposal.
precautions: Do not dismantle electronic devices unless you know proper handling.
Keep e-waste away from children and pets.
Avoid burning e-waste as it releases toxic fumes.
Separate hazardous components like batteries before disposal.
Handle broken electronics carefully to avoid cuts or chemical exposure.

Paints.title: How to Properly Dispose of Paints
steps: Check the Type of Paint: Determine if the paint is water-based (latex) or oil-based. Water-based paints are easier to recycle, while oil-based paints are considered hazardous waste.
Use Up Leftover Paint: Try to finish leftover paint on small projects. If not possible, consider donating it to community centers, schools, or theater groups.

Store Paint Properly: Keep paint in its original container with the lid tightly closed. Label the container with the paint type and color for easy identification. Store in a cool, dry place away from children, pets, and heat sources.

Locate a Recycling or Collection Center: Search for local hazardous waste collection facilities or paint recycling centers. Many municipalities or hardware stores have designated drop-off points for unused paint.

Prepare Paint for Drop-off: For water-based paints, you can solidify leftover liquid using kitty litter, sawdust, or commercial paint hardeners if the center allows it. Keep containers sealed to prevent leaks.
Transport Paint Safely: Carry the paint containers upright in a secure box or bag. Avoid tilting or shaking to prevent spills.
Hand Over to Staff or Place in Bin: At the center, hand the paint to staff or place it in the designated area. Follow any specific instructions given by the recycling center.
Spread Awareness: Encourage friends, family, and neighbors to recycle paint responsibly. Avoid pouring paint down drains or into regular trash.
precautions: Do not pour paint into drains, toilets, or the environment.
Avoid mixing paint with other household waste.
Use gloves when handling oil-based or unknown paints.
Keep paint containers sealed to prevent leaks and fumes.
Never burn paint, as it releases toxic chemicals into the air.
